Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

brand noun

a maker’s name or mark on goods

also brand name, make, label, trademark, brands, what brand?

classical

Cic. Brut. 287: eae notae sunt optimae, those brands are the best (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 2.3.8: interiōre notā Falernī

1Lewis & Short: “a mark on a wine-cask, to denote the quality of the wine … hence, a sort, kind, quality”, and of notae in Cic. Brut. 287, “wines of those brands”. The use of a maker’s brand of anything else is ours.

nota1, notae f.

noun, first declension

a brand, a make; a sort, a quality

The mark on a wine jar that told its vintage and quality, and so a brand of wine and any sort or quality of thing: secundae notae mel, second-grade honey (Col. 9.15.3; Lewis & Short). Its other senses are a mark or sign of any kind, a letter or shorthand sign, and the censor’s mark of disgrace.

Other words

  • signum, signī n. — a maker’s stamp, a trademark

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Mart. 13.30.1: cāseus Etruscae signātus imāgine Lūnae

    A mark or seal pressed into a thing; Martial’s cheese from Luna came signātus, stamped with the city’s moon, as Roman bricks, lamps and pots were stamped with the maker’s name.

Examples

  • seu tē in remōtō grāmine per diēs fēstōs reclīnātum beāris interiōre notā Falernī

    or whether, stretched out on the grass in some quiet spot on holidays, you treat yourself to a Falernian of an older brandHor. C. 2.3.6–8

  • cāseus Etruscae signātus imāgine Lūnae praestābit puerīs prandia mīlle tuīs

    a cheese stamped with the moon of Etruscan Luna will give your boys a thousand lunchesMart. 13.30.1–2

See also goods, new, company, advertisement.

SourcesLewis & Short: nota · Lewis & Short: signum

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
